AccountLifecycleStatus.description:
NOTE: If you update this, also update UserDomainAppLifecycleStatus

DISCOVERED             - Account discovered through accountfinding. Could be noisy.

STAGED                 - An account that has been queued for provisioning, but is not
                         provisioned yet. Relevant for Apps where provisioning is async
                         (eg. Okta, OneLogin).

ACCESS_CREATED         - When an account has been provisioned but not accessed.

ACTIVE                 - A live, active, accessible account.

SUSPENDED              - The user can no longer access the account, the license may or may not
                         be removed. The account can be recovered.

DEPROVISIONED          - The user can no longer access the account, the license was removed,
                         and the account cannot be recovered.

ARCHIVED               - The user can no longer access the account, the license may or may not
                         be removed. The account can be recovered.

MANUALLY_REMOVED       - The user can no longer access the account, the license is presumably
                         removed, but all of this was done manually

ACCESS_REMOVED         - The user can no longer access the account, but a license may still
                         exist. This is the case when we remove access through Okta but not a
                         direct integration

NON_CORPORATE_ACCOUNT  - The account doesn't exist, or is a personal employee account.

WAITING_MANUAL_REMOVAL - Waiting manual removal, someone was requested to remove the user access
                         from the App, and we are waiting for an answer about it.

AppInputCreate.description:
Body of `POST /apps`: create a custom app, or connect an integration.

One flat model serves both operations (a request-body union would generate
poorly into SDK/Terraform clients). Providing `app_class_id` switches the
request from "create a custom app" to "connect an integration"; the model
validator enforces the fields each mode requires.

app_class_id.description: Canonical identifier of an integration to connect, e.g. `okta.com`. Providing it switches this request from creating a custom app to connecting that integration using `auth`/`settings`. Must be an integration Lumos supports for your domain; an unknown value is rejected with 400.
app_class_id.title: App Class Id

auth.description: Credentials for the integration being connected, as a JSON object — **all secrets go here**. The accepted keys depend on the integration and are validated server-side. Some integrations connect in-band from these credentials (e.g. an `api_key`, or an OAuth `client_id`/`client_secret`); others require browser consent and are finished in the Lumos UI — for those, send `{}`. Missing or wrong-shaped credentials are rejected with 400; credentials the third party rejects return 502. Only used with `app_class_id`.
auth.title: Auth

Most integrations use a flat object with credential keys at the top level; some nest credentials under named groups when the integration supports multiple authentication methods — mirror that nesting in the connect request. Some integrations require a manually-set instance id as `app_instance_identifier` (e.g. an Okta domain); others derive it from the credentials during connect. post.description:
Create a new access review campaign.

The review's initial status depends on whether apps are provided and whether a `target_launch_date` is set:

- **With apps**: the review starts in `IN_PREPARATION` while account and entitlement snapshots are taken. Status automatically transitions to `IN_PROGRESS` once snapshotting completes.
- **Without apps**: the review is created directly in `IN_PROGRESS`.
- **With a `target_launch_date`**: the review is held for that date in `SCHEDULED`, or `SCHEDULED_IN_PREPARATION` while its apps are snapshotted, and returns to `SCHEDULED` once snapshotting completes. A daily job launches it on the date, moving it to `IN_PROGRESS`.

A `recurrence_config` or `recurrence_days_frequency` takes effect only alongside a `target_launch_date`; sent without one it is rejected.

Poll `GET /access_reviews/{id}` to observe the status transition. To add apps after creation, use `POST /access_reviews/{id}/apps` (allowed on any status except `COMPLETED`).

400.description: Validation error — the request violated a business rule (e.g. duplicate review name, deadline in the past, review not in the required status for this operation).

403.description: Forbidden — the caller lacks permission for this change. Creating a review requires the `access_reviews.create` permission on the domain. Organization admins and App Admins have it, and a custom role can grant it. Changing an existing review requires `access_reviews.manage` on that review. Organization admins and the review's owners have it, and a custom role can grant it.

404.description: Not found — the referenced review / app does not exist.

get.description:
Get available scope filter options for a domain app or ARDA.

post.description:
**Complete a task** — transition any task to `COMPLETED` by applying its unique
completion action. For approval tasks this is the "approve" primitive.

Common uses:

- **Approve an access request** (task with `task_category=APPROVAL` and `product_area=APPSTORE`).
- **Mark a non-approval task done** when it exposes exactly one action that transitions
  to `COMPLETED` (e.g. acknowledging a manual provisioning step). Tasks with multiple
  possible completion actions should use `POST /tasks/{task_id}/perform-action` instead.

This endpoint resolves the unique action on the task that transitions it to `COMPLETED`
and applies it on behalf of the caller. The caller must be an assignee of the task (or a
domain admin). There is no request body.

Responses:

- `204 No Content` — task completed.
- `403 Forbidden` — caller is not authorized to act on the task.
- `409 Conflict` — task is already in the requested status (safe to treat as idempotent).
- `404 Not Found` — task does not exist in this domain, or the Tasks API is not enabled.

To deny instead of approve, use [`POST /tasks/{task_id}/dismiss`](#dismiss-task). For
tasks that expose custom workflow actions (not approvals), use
[`POST /tasks/{task_id}/perform-action`](#perform-task-action).

post.description:
**Dismiss a task** — transition any task to `DISMISSED` by applying its unique
dismissal action. For approval tasks this is the "deny / reject" primitive; for
non-approval tasks it cancels the task without performing its work.

Common uses:

- **Deny an access request**.
- **Cancel a non-approval task** (e.g. dismiss an error task once the underlying issue is
  handled out-of-band). Tasks with multiple possible dismissal actions should use
  `POST /tasks/{task_id}/perform-action` instead.

Resolves the unique action on the task that transitions it to `DISMISSED` and applies it
on behalf of the caller. The caller must be an assignee of the task (or a domain admin).
There is no request body.

Responses:

- `204 No Content` — task dismissed.
- `403 Forbidden` — caller is not authorized to act on the task.
- `409 Conflict` — task is already in the requested status.
- `404 Not Found` — task does not exist in this domain, or the Tasks API is not enabled.

To approve instead of deny, use [`POST /tasks/{task_id}/complete`](#complete-task).

workflow-specific actions beyond approve/deny.

For approval tasks, prefer `POST /tasks/{task_id}/complete` or
`POST /tasks/{task_id}/dismiss` — those endpoints are simpler and do not require
discovering the action type.

Use this endpoint only when the task exposes custom actions. Discover the available

`transition_to` is optional — if the action has exactly one possible target status, it
is inferred. Pass it explicitly when an action can transition to more than one status.

- `204 No Content` — action performed.
- `400 Bad Request` — unknown action type or invalid transition.
- `403 Forbidden` — caller is not authorized to act on the task.
- `409 Conflict` — task is already in the requested status.

tags.description:
Create and manage access review campaigns — scheduled reviews of who has access to what
across your connected apps.

**Typical workflow for creating a review:**

1. `GET /apps` — find the domain app UUIDs you want to review.
2. `GET /access_reviews/scope_options?domain_app_id={id}` — discover available scope
   filters (employment status, team, last login, etc.). Each returned `items` entry is a
   ready-to-POST `scope_filters` payload; datetime and custom-attribute groups instead
   expose a `filter_input_template`.
3. `POST /access_reviews` with `apps` (optionally with `scope_filters` per app) —
   creates the campaign.
4. `GET /access_reviews/{id}` — poll until `status` transitions from `IN_PREPARATION`
   to `IN_PROGRESS`.

**After creation:**

- `POST /access_reviews/{id}/apps` — add more apps while `status != COMPLETED`.
- `PATCH /access_reviews/{id}` — update name / deadline / owner, or per-ARDA
  `scope_filters` and removal action.
- `DELETE /access_reviews/{id}` — soft-delete the whole campaign.
- `DELETE /access_reviews/{id}/apps/{arda_id}` — soft-delete a single app from the
  campaign.

All endpoints require an API token with the `access_reviews.create` or
`access_reviews.view` permission (Access Review Administrator or App Admin role).
tags.name: Access Reviews

tags.description:
**Tasks** are work items emitted by Lumos workflows — things that need a human (or an
automated caller) to make a decision or perform a step before the workflow can proceed.
Typical examples:

- An access request is waiting on an approver's decision.
- A provisioning or deprovisioning step needs manual fulfillment.
- An error needs acknowledgement.

Each task carries two classification fields you can filter on:

- **`task_category`** — what kind of decision or step the task represents. Values:
  `APPROVAL`, `PROVISIONING`, `DEPROVISIONING`, `ERROR`.
- **`product_area`** — which Lumos product surface emitted the task. Values:
  `APPSTORE`, `ACCESS_REVIEWS`, `MOVER`, `ATTRIBUTE_SYNC`, `OFFBOARDING`, `ONBOARDING`,
  `PLATFORM`, `SAVINGS`.

### Which endpoint should I call?

- **To approve or deny an access request**, use `POST /tasks/{task_id}/complete`
  (approve) or `POST /tasks/{task_id}/dismiss` (deny).
- **To find pending approval tasks**, call
  `GET /tasks?task_category=APPROVAL&product_area=APPSTORE&status=PENDING` (access
  requests).
- **Only use `POST /tasks/{task_id}/perform-action`** for tasks that expose custom workflow
  actions. Discover those actions via `GET /tasks/{task_id}/actions`. Approval tasks do not
  require this endpoint — `complete` and `dismiss` are the right primitives.

For a full walkthrough with `curl` and Python examples, see the
[Tasks API How-To](https://docs.lumos.com/reference/list_tasks_tasks_get) guide.
tags.name: Tasks

tags.description:
An integration is a service Lumos knows how to connect to, identified by an `app_class_id` such as
`okta.com` or `workspace.google.com`. This is the catalog you connect *from*. Apps you have
already connected are read through the Apps endpoints.

Only connectable integrations appear here. Software discovered in your environment that has no
Lumos integration behind it is excluded.

### Discovering how to connect

1. `GET /v1/integrations?query=google` to find the integration. The filter matches both the
   `app_class_id` and the display name, so `google` returns `workspace.google.com` and
   `cloud.google.com`.
2. `GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}/connection-schema` for the JSON schema of the `auth` and
   `settings` fields it expects.
3. `POST /v1/apps` with those values.

Step 2 is the point of this group: it lets you build a connect form without hardcoding one
credential shape per integration.

`GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}` and the connection schema return 404 for any integration the
list leaves out. The connection schema also returns 404 for an integration whose schema Lumos
cannot describe yet.
tags.name: Integrations

tags.description:
An app is an integration you have connected, one per connected instance of a service. Your Okta
tenant is an app. A second Slack workspace is a second app.

### Connecting one

1. `GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}/connection-schema` to see which `auth` and `settings`
   keys the integration expects.
2. `POST /v1/apps` with those credentials. Apps whose credentials validate right away connect, and
   their first sync waits for an admin to review match rules. It starts from the Lumos UI, or from
   `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync` with `skip_first_sync_review: true`. Apps that need browser
   consent are finished in the Lumos UI.
3. `GET /v1/apps/{app_uuid}` to follow the first sync. `sync_status` shows the state of the
   app's most recent sync. A sync started with `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync` also returns an
   operation, which you poll with `GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}`.
4. `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync` to resync later. Only one sync runs per app at a time, so a
   second request while one is in flight returns 409.

Rotate credentials with `PATCH /v1/apps/{app_uuid}`, which also updates an app's metadata.
`POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:disconnect` drops the stored credentials and returns the app to a
connectable state; `DELETE /v1/apps/{app_uuid}` removes the app outright.

### Reading apps

`expand` is opt-in and evaluated per field: ask for `admins`, `custom_attributes`,
`appstore_settings`, or any of the three workflow fields. A field you lack permission to read is
left out of the response instead of failing the whole request, so a 200 does not prove every field
you asked for came back.

To list only the connected apps you manage through the API, combine `connection_source=API` with
`disconnected=false`.

### Bound workflows

Each app carries three bindings: an approval workflow, a default provisioning workflow, and a
default deprovisioning workflow. The two `default_` workflows are the ones that entitlements on
the app fall back to. To bind a workflow to one entitlement instead, use the Entitlements
endpoints.
tags.name: Apps

tags.description:
An entitlement is a grantable unit of access on an app: a role, a license tier, a group, a
permission. Accounts hold entitlements.

- `POST /v1/entitlements` creates a requestable entitlement on an app.
- `GET /v1/apps/{app_uuid}/entitlements` lists the entitlements on one app.
- `GET /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}/accounts` lists who currently holds one.
- `PATCH /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}` renames it. `label` is the only field you can change
  today, and sending any other field returns 400.
- `DELETE /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}` refuses while the entitlement is still held,
  returning 409 with an `active_accounts` count.

### Per-entitlement workflows

An entitlement can have its own approval override, provisioning workflow, and deprovisioning
workflow, bound to it rather than to the whole app. Each has a GET and a PUT.

Not every entitlement supports them. An entitlement with no request configuration behind it
returns 404 with `Workflows are not available for this entitlement.` on all six.
tags.name: Entitlements

tags.description:
An account is a person's presence inside a connected app. Accounts arrive through sync; you cannot
create one through this API.

`GET /v1/accounts/{account_uuid}/entitlements` lists what one account holds. It reads the same
relationship as `GET /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}/accounts`, from the account's side rather
than the entitlement's.
tags.name: Accounts

tags.description:
A workflow is a reusable definition of the steps Lumos runs to approve a request, provision access,
or deprovision it. Create the definition here, then bind it to an app or an entitlement through
their own workflow endpoints.

### Building one

1. `GET /v1/workflow-steps?app_id={app_uuid}&type={workflow type}` to discover the steps available
   for that app in the type of workflow you will create, each with the input schema it accepts.
   Without `type`, it lists only the steps every workflow type accepts.
2. `POST /v1/workflows` with the steps you want.
3. Bind it, for example with `PUT /v1/apps/{app_uuid}/default-provisioning-workflow`.

`type` and `app_id` are fixed at creation. `PUT /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}` returns 400 for a
change to either.

### Workflows this API cannot describe

Some workflows Lumos builds for you, including the out-of-the-box provisioning defaults, contain
steps with no public representation. `GET /v1/workflows` skips them, so a page can hold fewer items
than `page_size` while more results remain. Treat an absent `next_page_token`, not a short page, as
the end of the list. Binding one of these to an app or entitlement returns 400.
tags.name: Workflows

tags.description:
Custom attributes are the extra fields your organization keeps on users. These endpoints read
their *definitions*, not the values stored against any particular user.

`GET /v1/custom-attribute-definitions` returns one entry per label, unified across every app that
supplies it. Narrow the list with `source_type` to tell attributes synced from an app apart from
ones your team created, or with `app_id` to see only what a single app supplies.
tags.name: Custom Attribute Definitions

tags.description:
Knowledge entries are the documents and notes Lumos agents draw on when they answer access
questions. Each entry carries a title, body, tags, and product scopes, plus an optional file
attachment.

Because of that attachment, create and update send `multipart/form-data` rather than JSON. On
update, tag and scope lists replace what was there instead of appending, and `clear_attachment=true`
removes an existing file without uploading a replacement.

`DELETE` archives rather than destroys. The entry stops appearing in list results and stays
recoverable.

Pages here are small: `page_size` defaults to 10 and is clamped to 25.
tags.name: Knowledge
